c.tagline: Africa's cocoa isle where the equator meets the Atlantic.

taxi.fareNote: Private taxis negotiate a fixed price before departure (roughly $10 for a 10km trip); shared hiace minivans cover the same routes for a fraction of the cost but leave only once full.

emergency.note: Medical facilities are very limited; serious injuries or illnesses typically require evacuation to Portugal or elsewhere. Comprehensive travel insurance with medevac coverage is strongly recommended.

religion.r: Evangelical/Protestant (Adventist, Assembly of God, New Apostolic, etc.)

hood_landmark.Centro (Downtown): Sé Catedral de Nossa Senhora da Graça, São Tomé

avoid.reason: Petty theft happens on beaches and around the central market, so avoid flashing valuables and skip poorly lit streets after dark.

hood_desc: The historic downtown core around Ana Chaves Bay, with the cathedral, fortress-museum and central market within walking distance; suits first-time visitors who want to explore on foot and stay close to restaurants and shops.

A quiet beachfront strip right beside the airport runway, home to the city's most polished resort-style hotels; ideal for travelers who want easy transfers, a pool, and sea views without needing a taxi.
A laid-back fishing village on the eastern edge of the city with a long black-sand beach and a slower pace; good for those wanting a local, coastal feel away from downtown bustle.
A dense, authentic residential neighborhood just south of the center, popular with volunteers, NGO workers and budget travelers wanting an affordable base close to everything.

The upscale southern seafront avenue near the Presidential Palace, home to São Tomé's top hotels and ocean-view dining; suited to travelers wanting comfort within a short walk or taxi ride of downtown.

water.note: Outdated infrastructure makes tap water unsafe; stick to bottled or treated water.

transit.pay: Fares for hiaces and city buses are paid in cash (dobra) directly to the driver or a conductor when boarding or alighting; there is no smart-card or app-based payment system. Fares are fixed per route rather than metered, so having small notes helps.
transit.hours: Hiaces and buses generally operate from around 6am to 7-8pm; there is little to no public transport after dark, so taxis or pre-arranged drivers are the main after-hours option.
transit.note: Transport is informal and route-based rather than scheduled; vehicles depart from markets and central stops once full. Most visitors combine hiaces for short hops with taxis or rental cars for flexibility.

tip.r: Tipping is not deeply rooted in local custom but is increasingly appreciated at tourist-oriented hotels and restaurants; rounding up or leaving 5-10% is a welcome gesture, not an obligation.
